analysis:
Examined the three changed files: StatusCommand.swift (lines 148-153 head), UnenrollCommand+KeepServing.swift (lines 21-27 head) and StatusCommandRunTests.swift (new test at the end).

Status now computes two values from the daemon state file. `displayedProviderAuthorization` is used for display and `currentProviderAuthorization` is used as `removalAuthorization`. Both are passed to `ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.summary(..., removalAuthorization:, now:)`. The intent is that an unexpired lease whose renewal is late still shows as App Attest authorized, while the MDM removal guidance requires fresh coordinator readiness. This only changes how a status line is rendered, so it is a display-only change.

The unenroll keep-serving path is unchanged in its gating. `removalReady(authorization, now:)` still guards on the strict `currentProviderAuthorization` (line 23), and the readiness is re-read before guidance is shown (lines 61-67). The only change is the signature of the error summary, which receives `removalAuthorization: authorization`. The removal gate is not weakened, so T-053 (stale authorization surviving revocation) and T-057 are not regressed there.

The new test asserts that a late renewal with an unexpired lease keeps the Authorization line, does not fall back to the legacy Trust line, and does not offer removal.

Limits: the definitions of `displayedProviderAuthorization`, `currentProviderAuthorization` and `ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.summary` are outside the supplied evidence. I could not confirm that `displayedProviderAuthorization` still enforces the coordinator URL, expiry and revocation binding. It must not display authorization after expiry or revocation, since that would misstate trust (T-052, T-053, T-058). The next pass should check those definitions in ProviderCore and confirm that status-only output does not feed any serving or removal decision. The display is local-only and derived from a state file the same-UID user can already edit, so no new boundary is crossed.
